international: Non-EU students whose family lives abroad do not use an Italian ISEE: they submit documents issued by the authorities of the country where income was earned, translated into Italian by the Italian diplomatic authorities.
Documents must show household composition, each member's 2025 gross income, property and movable assets at 31 December 2025, and rent paid.
Missing documents or translations lead to automatic exclusion.
Students from MUR's 'particularly poor countries' list may instead provide a certificate from the Italian representation in their country.

international: Non-EU students provide complete income and asset documentation issued by the authorities of the countries where income was earned and assets are held — self-declarations are not accepted.
Documents must be translated and legalised or apostilled, with values in local currency (converted at the Bank of Italy's 2025 average rate).
They must include family composition, 2025 income of each adult member and property at 31 December 2025.
Upload them in the ER.GO user dossier by the application deadline — missing documents make you ineligible.

international: Non-resident students' finances are assessed through an ISEEUP signed at a DiSCo partner CAF.
The CAF needs official documents from the Italian diplomatic authorities in your home country, translated into Italian, showing household members, 2024 income, property and rent.
No self-declarations, affidavits or sworn statements are accepted, and total household income cannot be zero.
Students from 'particularly poor countries' may use consular documents legalised by the Prefecture instead.
